newsitem.title: USA: Mixed views on Q3 PC shipments, but Q4 pickup seen.
newsitem.headline: Mixed views on Q3 PC shipments, but Q4 pickup seen.

text.p: The picture for worldwide personal computer demand is either half-empty or half-full, depending on which of two surveys of third quarter PC shipments by leading market research firms one reads.
International Data said Monday that year-over-year growth in PC shipments slackened to 12 percent, the slowest pace in five years, based on its preliminary third quarter statistics.
But Dataquest said PC shipments rose 16.3 percent in the third quarter versus a year-ago, growth it called "steady."
But both firms expect PC shipments to pick up the pace in the fourth quarter and grow about 20 percent, year-to-year.
The different conclusions about the third quarter reflect IDC's emphasis on U.S. PC shipment data versus Dataquest's focus on the more robust international shipments.

The IDC figure of 12 percent reflects only PC shipments to the United States, the world's largest market. In its own survey, Dataquest said U.S. PC shipments rose 12.5 percent, or roughly the same level as reported in the IDC survey.
Worldwide, IDC said third quarter unit shipments rose 16 percent in the third quarter, about what Dataquest reported.
However, both IDC and Dataquest concurred on the winners and losers among top computer makers in the latest quarter.

Both said Compaq Computer Corp once again led the market in the third quarter in terms of PC shipments, while Packard Bell-NEC Corp and Apple Computer Inc saw declines compared with very strong year-ago periods.

The two firms agreed that International Business Machines Corp is making progress on some of its long-standing operational difficulties and stands a good chance of boosting market share this year for the first time since 1993.
Another vendor doing extremely well is Dell, which grew more than 50 percent in the quarter, both surveys agreed.
Apple also benefited from strong U.S. educational sales, which set a company record, but the rest of its product lines were less successful, IDC said.
Sales of consumer desktops were particularly weak versus last year, when the company shipped extraordinary numbers of low-end systems late in the quarter, it said.
Both firms agreed that Apple's recent moves to expand its consumer line and slash prices should help its sales rebound in the fourth quarter.
IDC said growth for many PC vendors was sluggish in Europe, where economic conditions have been dampening demand.
The sales increase was stronger in Japan, and in the Asia/Pacific area, where economic expansion is leading to rising purchases of PCs, according to IDC.

The PC market tracker said the U.S. market continued its pattern of moderating, yet still substantial, growth in the third quarter, boosting confidence that the crucial fourth quarter will be a good one.

IDC said that while U.S. third quarter year-over-year growth was modest at 12 percent, the major reason for the slowdown appeared to be that last year's third quarter was somewhat artificially inflated.
PC makers showed greater caution in the recent third quarter compared with the same period a year ago, IDC said.
In the 1995 third quarter, a number of vendors, especially Apple and Packard Bell, had shipped large quantities of PCs to retailers in anticipation of strong holiday sales.

The rise in shipments led to an inventory over-supply crunch last year that appears to have encouraged greater caution this year, when PC vendors seem to be holding back on shipments to get a better feel for customer demand, IDC said.
"PC vendors are being extra careful this year, after getting burned by excess inventory at the end of 1995," said Eric Lewis, an IDC personal computer systems analyst.
Still, Lewis said IDC expects that "Shipments will pick up as we move through the fourth quarter, leading to a happy holiday season for the PC industry."
